"For those who fear the painful punishment" (للذين يخافون العذاب الأليم): that is, the punishment of the Hereafter, so that they do not commit their abominable deed.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Abraham and his guests from among the angels. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 51, verses 38–46:

Explanation of the words:

"And in Musa (Moses) when We sent him to Fir'awn (Pharaoh)": that is, he denied him and disbelieved, so We drowned him and those with him, a sign like the sign of Sodom.

"With clear authority": that is, with a strong, manifest proof, namely the hand and the staff.

"But he turned away with his supporters": that is, he turned away from faith together with the men of his people.

"And said, 'A sorcerer or a madman'": that is, Pharaoh said concerning Musa, "A sorcerer or a madman."

"So We cast them into the sea": that is, We threw them into the sea, and they drowned, every one of them.

"And he was blameworthy": that is, he came with what deserves blame, for he was the one who exposed a whole army to destruction, in addition to his claim to lordship and his denial of Musa and Harun (Aaron), who were two messengers.

"And in 'Ad": that is, and in the destruction of 'Ad there is a sign, a mark of Our power and Our governance.

"The barren wind": that is, the wind in which there is no good, because it does not carry rain nor fertilize trees, and it is the ad-Dabur (the western wind). This is due to the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "I was helped by the east wind (aṣ-Ṣabā), and 'Ad were destroyed by the ad-Dabur, which is the western wind in the Hijaz."

"It leaves nothing that it passes over": from a soul or from property.

"Except that it makes it like the rameem": that is, the decayed, crumbling.

"And in Thamud": that is, and in the destruction of Thamud there is a sign indicating the power of Allah and His hatred for disbelief and criminality.

"When it was said to them": that is, after they hamstrung the she-camel, "Enjoy yourselves until the end of your term, after three days."

"Then the thunderbolt seized them": that is, three days after they hamstrung the she-camel.

"So they were not able to rise up": that is, they were unable to stand up when the punishment descended upon them.

"And the people of Nuh (Noah) before": that is, and in the destruction of the people of Nuh by the flood there is a sign, and a greater sign.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, "And in Musa..." — when He mentioned the destruction of the people of Lut and made it a sign indicating His power and a mark that informs the intelligent person of His vengeance upon those who disbelieved in Him and disobeyed Him, He mentioned here, in these nine verses of this context, four other signs, by which the people of faith who fear the Day of Reckoning are guided. He, mighty is He, said: "And in Musa, son of 'Imran, the prophet of the Children of Israel, when We sent him to Fir'awn, king of the Copts in Egypt, with clear authority," that is, with a strong, manifest proof, as clear as the authority is strong and evident, which was the staff. But he did not respond to the call of truth, so he turned away with his supporters, that is, with his army on which he relied and depended. He said concerning Musa, the messenger sent to him, "He is a sorcerer or a madman." So We took vengeance upon him after his persistence in disbelief and wrongdoing, and We cast them, that is, threw them into the sea, the Yam, and they perished by drowning. In this deed which We did to Fir'awn, because he denied, there is one of the most evident signs.

His saying, may He be exalted, "And in 'Ad," when We sent to them their brother Hud, who called them to worship Allah alone and to abandon worshipping anything other than Him, but they denied him, "when We sent upon them the barren wind," which carries no rain and fertilizes no trees, "that leaves nothing that it passes over, from souls or property, except that it makes it like the rameem, the decayed, crumbling." In this destruction there is one of the greatest signs indicating the power of Allah, which necessitates His lordship and worship, and which entails His power over resurrection and recompense on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, may He be exalted, "And in Thamud," when We sent to them their brother Salih, who called them to worship Allah alone and to abandon shirk, but they denied him and demanded from him a sign indicating his truthfulness. So Allah gave them the she-camel as a sign, but they hamstrung her, out of contempt and denial, "when it was said to them, 'Enjoy yourselves until a appointed time,'" that is, until the end of the term set for their destruction. Instead of believing, submitting, and worshipping and affirming the oneness of Allah, they defied the command of their Lord and became arrogant, haughty, "so the thunderbolt seized them," the thunderbolt of punishment, while they were looking with their own eyes at death snatching at them, "so they were not able to rise up," from their seats, while they were kneeling on their knees, "nor were they able to defend themselves." In the destruction of Thamud, the people of al-Hijr, there is a sign for those who fear the painful punishment, so that they do not do their deed and thus do not suffer their destruction.

His saying, may He be exalted, "And the people of Nuh before, indeed they were a people of defiant transgression." That is, in Our sending Nuh to his people, their denial of him, their persistence in shirk, disbelief and denial, then Our destruction of them by the flood and Our deliverance of the believers, is a sign among the greatest signs indicating the existence of Allah, His lordship, and His divinity over the worlds, and entailing His power over resurrection and recompense, which the atheists insist on denying so that they may continue their defiance and corruption without reproach of conscience, shame, fear, or dread.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of tawhid (the oneness of Allah), prophethood, and resurrection, for the verses contain proofs of all of these.

2- The power of Allah is above every power, since every power on earth is what He created and granted.

3- Accusing the people of truth of falsehood in order to repel the truth and refuse to accept it is almost a human custom in every time and place.

4- Among the causes of destruction is arrogance toward the command of Allah, that is, not submitting to accept it, and defiance of obedience to Him and to His messengers.
